description.narrative:
WHO's General Programme of Work (henceforth GPW) is a strategic framework that sets a high-level roadmap and agenda for WHO's work on global health. Each edition of GPW describes the Organization's priorities and strategic direction for a specified period. GPW also provides a framework for resource allocation and decision-making for WHO. GPW is developed in consultation with Member States, experts and stakeholders across the global health ecosystem and beyond for multi-year periods. It is approved by the World Health Assembly. The currently active strategic framework is GPW14, guiding WHO's work for the period 2025-2028.
The GPW is also the basis for WHOs biennial Programme Budget, which translates the GPW into the organisation's strategic deliverables and budget requirements for a biennium. The Programme Budget sets out the details of what will be achieved and indicates the resources required for their achievement. The WHO Results Framework in addition to measuring progress towards GPW goals and targets, informs WHO's own reporting on results which are summarized and communicated through the WHO Results Reports and the WHO Programme Budget Portal.
The Programme budget 20262027 utilizes the integrated results framework from the Fourteenth General Programme of Work (GPW14).
GPW14 builds on the strengths and learnings of its predecessor, GPW13 recommendations from the Evaluation of GPW 13.
The overarching action oriented vision of GPW14 is to promote, provide and protect the health and well-being of all people, everywhere. By 2028, WHO, together with Member States and all other key partners, will ensure that, of the projected 8.4 billion people living in the world, 6 billion will be enabled to live healthier lives, 5 billion will be able to access health services without financial hardship and 7 billion will be protected from health emergencies.
GPW14 complements GPW13s Triple Billion model with Six Strategic Objectives, that describe how the action mission will be delivered.These objectives define what the world must achieve from 20252028 to improve health outcomes.
1. Respond to climate change 2. Address determinants and root causes of ill health 3. Advance PHC and essential system capacities 4. Improve service coverage financial protection 5. Prevent, mitigate and prepare for all hazards 6. Rapidly detect and sustain emergency response
These objectives directly serve the action oriented mission.
